headline: Why haven't I found my soulmate where I am?
note: generated from REVIEW-new-voice.md — not a wired draft

a: You turned the Magician. Three backs, nothing to go on, and yours was the one who came ready.
Look at his table. It's full, and it stands on open grass.
You asked why you haven't found your soulmate where you are. What catches me is that the table is full wherever it stands.
The part that doesn't fit is that nobody has come. And you've started to think the problem is where you are.
The hold is constant, and it doesn't come and go. I don't think it began with you.
Let me look closer at what this is…
b: You turned the Hanged Man. Nothing showed which was which, and you took the one held at one ankle.
Look at the rope. One ankle, and the rest of him is loose.
You asked why you haven't found your soulmate where you are. One rope holds the whole of it in place.
Still, nobody has come. And the question has turned into whether you're in the wrong spot.
Something is standing in the way of it, close in. I don't think this began with you.
Let me look closer at what's behind this…
c: You turned the Fool. Face down, all three, and you chose the one already walking.
Look at his feet. One is off the ground, and the other isn't far behind.
You asked why you haven't found your soulmate where you are. What I'm looking at is a step being taken.
But nobody has come. And you're the one asking whether you're standing in the wrong place.
Something turns up right as that step comes down. I don't think it started with you.
Let me look closer at what it is…
